$comment: Audited external facts cited in shipped guidance, and where each is cited.
What belongs here: facts whose *currency* matters — a coverage matrix tied to a
release, a provider major whose behaviour the guidance describes, an action
pinned by SHA in shipped CI. Drift in those needs a decision.
What does not: values whose *form* matters rather than their currency. The
worked mise.toml in docs/setup.md names terraform, gh and jq versions that the
document itself labels examples — the requirement is that a reader pins an exact
version, not that it be the newest one. Tracking them produced a red nightly
every few weeks with no decision attached, and a check that cries wolf is how
the incident behind #24 stayed invisible.
Two checks run against this file. Coherence (offline, part of `make check`):
every `cited_as` string must still appear in each doc that cites it, the
expected number of times, so the manifest cannot drift away from the prose.
Freshness (network, nightly): `audited` is compared against the current
upstream release.
`cited_as` exists because `audited` alone is not searchable: a bare major like
"5" matches a numbered step or `Terraform 1.5+`. An item may be
{"text": ..., "count": n} to require an exact number of occurrences, so
updating one of several mentions cannot pass while the rest go stale.
A citation may include prose, such as a matrix's provenance date, when that prose
goes stale with the version. There is no separate date field: one mechanism only.
An entry with `audited_sha` also has that SHA checked against the commit its
audited tag resolves to, so a version bump cannot leave a stale pinned commit.
`sources` are all machine-readable and readable unauthenticated.
HCP API endpoint paths are not tracked here yet. An earlier version of this note
claimed HCP publishes no machine-readable API schema to diff them against; that is
wrong — hashicorp/go-tfe ships one at v2/openapi/spec.json, which is how #37 was
settled. Tracking paths against it is now possible and merely undone; see the issue
filed for it (#55) rather than treating this as impossible.

entries.name: cf-terraforming
entries.why_it_matters: The per-resource coverage matrix in import.md was audited against this release; newer ones may cover more or differ in generated HCL. Cited in four places, plus an abbreviated v0.29 claim and the matrix's 'September 2026' provenance date, all of which must move together.

entries.name: mise-action
entries.why_it_matters: Pinned by commit SHA in the CI example. The SHA is the value that runs; the version is only a comment. The nightly resolves the audited tag and requires the cited SHA to match it, so the two cannot be updated independently.

entries.name: cloudflare-provider-major
entries.why_it_matters: Guidance states behaviour specific to the v5 provider; a new major invalidates it.

entries.name: github-provider-major
entries.why_it_matters: Repository, branch-protection and label guidance is written against the v6 provider; a new major invalidates the resource shapes it describes.
